My friends, fellow citizens, believers in freedom,

We are gathered today at a crossroads. A moment that will define our generation and decide the future of liberty itself. For decades, we have been told that the path to a more just society lies in creating new laws, new categories, new protections for specific groups. We were told this was the path to equality.

I am here today to tell you that we have been led astray. The path we are on does not lead to equality. It leads to a new kind of segregation. It does not lead to justice. It leads to a hierarchy of grievance. And it does not lead to freedom. It leads to the shackling of the conscience and the erosion of the very bedrock of our society.

The great promise of this nation, the one that echoes in the Declaration of Independence and is enshrined in our Constitution, is breathtakingly simple and profoundly radical: that we are all created equal, and that we are all entitled to the same rights, the same dignity, the same protection under the law. One law, for all people.

But in recent years, a different philosophy has taken root. A philosophy that says we are not, in fact, equals. It says we are defined by our identities, our orientations, our internal feelings. And it says that some groups, because of these identities, deserve a special set of legal protections that others do not.

This is not equality. This is favoritism. This is a system that tells a small business owner that their faith, their conscience, their deeply held beliefs are secondary to the demands of the state. It forces them to choose between the soul of their business and the judgment of a courtroom. Is this the freedom our ancestors bled and died for? To live in fear that at any moment, your livelihood can be destroyed because you dare to live by your convictions?

This philosophy tells our daughters that their private spaces, their sports, their hard-won opportunities are not truly their own. It tells them that the word "woman," a reality as old as humanity itself, can be redefined by ideology, overnight, without their consent. This is not justice. This is an injustice against every single woman and girl who has ever fought for a place at the table.

And what has been the result of this grand experiment in social engineering? Has it brought us together? No! It has driven us apart. It has taught our children to see each other not as fellow human beings, as friends, as neighbors, but as members of competing tribes. It has created a chilling effect on free speech, where a single wrong word, a misplaced pronoun, can end a career and ruin a life.

I say, enough is enough!

We must be brave enough to say what we know in our hearts to be true. The path to a harmonious society is not through more division, but through more unity. It is not through more laws that separate us, but by reaffirming the one law that binds us all.

Therefore, I call for the complete and total repeal of all legal protections that are based specifically on sexual orientation and gender identity.

This is not an act of malice. It is an act of liberation! It is a declaration that we will return to the principle of judging one another by the content of our character, not the nature of our identity. It is a statement that our laws will once again be blind to our personal lives, but fiercely protective of our individual rights.

Imagine a future where the law is simple, clear, and fair to all. Where your business is protected because property rights are sacred for everyone. Where your job is secure based on your merit and your hard work, period. Where your children are taught to respect every single person, not because they belong to a protected class, but because they are a fellow human being deserving of dignity.

This is the future we can build. A future of true equality, where the state does not pick winners and losers. A future of profound freedom, where your conscience is your own. A future of unity, where we are no longer hyphenated Americans, but simply, Americans.

This will not be an easy fight. The forces that profit from our division will call us every name in the book. They will twist our words and question our motives. But we will not be silenced. We will stand together. We will fight for the soul of our nation. We will fight for a future where our children are free.

Let us reclaim the promise of this great land. Let us tear down these walls of legal segregation. Let us restore the sacred principle of one nation, under God, with liberty and justice for all.

Thank you, and God bless you.
